summary: The /yacht-mortgages/ page is a marketing/service page of the London broker Silver Oak Capital. According to the two productive searches, it presents yacht mortgages as secured loans where the vessel itself is the collateral, aimed at high-net-worth individuals (HNWIs) and corporate entities, with a focus on cross-border ownership arrangements that mainstream banks often decline, and on Western European / Mediterranean hubs (Monaco, Cote d'Azur, Italy, Netherlands). One verbatim sentence was recovered: 'Silver Oak Capital specialises in securing our clients' bespoke, tailored yacht finance for high-net-worth individuals (HNWIs) and corporate entities.' The search summaries also pulled in related content from sibling marine pages on the same site: typical loan structure (5-7 year term, balloon near 25% of principal, leasing as the alternative), a worked example (GBP 6m facility, 70% LTV, 3.5% fixed, 60 months, 20% balloon, 6 months' interest held on deposit), a charter/'commercial registration' mortgage point, pre-construction stage-payment finance (interest-only, refinanced into a marine mortgage or lease at launch), vessels typically over 20m, UK/Cayman/BVI/Maltese registries, SPV ownership for superyachts with personal guarantee, a 1.00% typical broker fee, and the Heesen case study (USD 14m, 60% LTV, 50m yacht, 10 years). Search [c] (standard, with 'loan to value') returned only generic third-party yacht-finance articles and nothing about Silver Oak Capital. No H1, meta description, section headings, FAQ, process steps or testimonials specific to this page were revealed.
